Within the bead layers, the fiber orientation is vastly random with clusters of highly oriented fibers spread throughout with some fiber swirling effects. Next, sample sets (3-1 to 3-3 and 4-1 to 4-3) extracted along the bead path are observed under microscope. A counterclockwise swirling effect of the fibers from the center of the bead to the edge of the bead is observed. Also, a considerable among of air is trapped within the printed bead. The fiber orientation at the intersection of the 4 print beads demonstrates a random pattern and varies amongst the 6 samples. The microstructure characterization revealed that the fiber orientation and distribution are different across and along bead paths. Overall, the fiber orientation is observed to be random within the samples composing of region with high alignment and low alignment. The highly aligned fiber layer between the two printed layers could be due to the building effect of the printing nozzle. Furthermore, the air trapped within the physical samples could lead to porosity upon compression. Various batches printed included the cubes for the purpose of base material characterization. The base material properties of the 3D printed metal from different printing batches were evaluated through tensile testing of SS-J3 specimens while monitoring with the Digital Image Correlation (DIC) system [8,9]. The DIC system was synchronized with the universal testing machine for the strain measurement. The stress-strain curves obtained for specimens from various batches are summarized in Fig. 5.2.1. Surface roughness measurements The surface roughness the samples are measured using the cubes printed along with the specimens in each batch of the binder jet printing. A cube from each of the four different batches are considered for surface roughness measurement and thus four cubes in total namely, C-02, C-23, C-32, and C-38. The cubes and the orientation definition for these samples are shown in Fig. 5.2.2. For the surface roughness, 16-17 measurements were made on each side of the cube.
